newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean futures end up on optimism.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean futures end up on optimism.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mostly up on Thursday on optimism over the market's direction following Wednesday's rises, traders said.
The most active July 1997 contract ended at 3,410 yuan ($411) per tonne, rising seven yuan. It opened at 3,412 yuan, hitting an intraday high of 3,420 and a low of 3,399 yuan.
May rose five to 3,350, September 23 to 3,430, November fell 15 to 3,415, January 1998 contract was unchanged at 3,430.
Combined volume rose to 26,000 tonnes from 23,000.
Traders said investors were optimistic about the short term market trend and the significant speculative buying that emerged was riding on the back of Wednesday's gains.
"Rises in both prices and trade volume indicate soybeans are likely to rise further in the short term," one trader said.
"But a lack of solid market-moving news will limit the potential of rises, leading to possible technical corrections," he added.
